2608.16949.title: Critical couplings of two dimensional Ising model on various lattices
2608.16949.summary:
- Unified fermionic‑field (Kac–Ward) formulation gives partition function as a determinant, reproducing exact critical couplings for square, honeycomb, triangular, kagomé, and dual kagomé lattices.
- Derives the full critical surface and low‑energy spectrum for the anisotropic kagomé lattice, and the anisotropic critical condition for its dual.
- Shows that the isotropic dice model has a relativistic massive low‑energy spectrum, with the mass vanishing at cosh(2J_c) = (1+√/

2608.16980.title: Hydrodynamization in 1D Bose gases at nonzero temperature
2608.16980.summary:
- Hydrodynamization coherence time is temperature‑independent in a 1D hard‑core Bose gas after a Bragg‑pulse quench.
- Increasing initial temperature shortens both the damping time of hydrodynamic oscillations and the prethermalization time.
- The effect is attributed to rapidity‑distribution broadening, motivating a nonzero‑temperature dephasing time.

2608.17009.title: PowderLine: a programmatic powder diffraction analysis application
2608.17009.summary:
- PowderLine packages full Rietveld or peak‑analysis refinements into a single, declarative, machine‑readable recipe.
- The recipe is validated against a versioned schema and executed via refinement software, yielding structured, machine‑readable results.
- This design enables seamless integration into interactive, scripted, and autonomous high‑throughput powder‑diffraction workflows.

2608.17040.title: Local magnetic resonance of scalar spin chirality
2608.17040.summary:
- Finite scalar spin chirality generates an orbital magnetic moment that has not been directly measured.
- Local spin‑resonance drives break cyclic symmetry, enabling chirality‑changing transitions that reveal the chiral orbital moment.
- Lindblad simulations predict observable signatures in locally addressable systems such as STM‑ESR, silicon donor spins, and quantum‑dot qubits.

2608.17061.title: Emissivity by Design: Geometric Mesh Inductance Governs Thermal Radiation in Metallic Nanowire Networks
2608.17061.summary:
- Emissivity is set by the geometric inductance of inter‑wire gaps, independent of wire length or percolation.
- A parameter‑free reactance \(X_L = Z_0(g/\lambda)\ln(2g/\pi D)\) captures diameter dependence, sheet‑resistance trends, and angular behavior.
- The model fits 56 silver‑nanowire samples (MAE , collapses data onto a universal curve, and predicts emissivity‑transmittance and spectral features for independent groups.

2608.17076.title: Hidden Ergodic Relaxation in the Quench Dynamics of a Bichromatic Mott Lattice
2608.17076.summary:
- Sudden quench of secondary lattice in a finite bichromatic Mott lattice drives coefficient and second R\'enyi entropies toward GOE predictions, indicating extensive Hilbert‑space spreading.
- Despite this entropy growth, local observables (momentum distribution, fragmentation, Glauber correlations) remain essentially unchanged, revealing hidden ergodic relaxation beneath persistent Mott order.
- An effective embedded random‑matrix model captures the crossover from restricted to extensive spreading, explaining the common relaxation trajectory independent of quench strength.

2608.17080.title: Controlling Structure and Properties of Vapor-Deposited Glasses of Organic Semiconductors: Recent Advances and Challenges
2608.17080.summary:
- Vapor‑deposited organic semiconductor glasses can be tuned by substrate temperature to vary density and molecular orientation.
- Optimized glass structures enhance OLED external quantum efficiency and device lifetime.
- Molecular simulations now reproduce experimental structures, enabling in‑silico design and guiding future research.

2608.17086.title: Rejuvenation versus overaging: The effect of cyclic loading/unloading on the segmental dynamics of PMMA glasses
2608.17086.summary:
- Cyclic tensile loading (5000 cycles, 003–007 strain, Tg – 10 K to Tg – 25 K) did not induce overaging in PMMA; segmental dynamics were unchanged or accelerated.
- Relaxation times after cycling returned to a common time scale comparable to the aging time, indicating retention of the material’s original age rather than full memory erasure.
- Probe reorientation measurements revealed deformation‐induced changes more sensitively than mechanical tests, yet no overaging was detected in either optical or mechanical data.

2608.17089.title: Over what length scale does an inorganic substrate perturb the structure of a glassy organic semiconductor?
2608.17089.summary:
- ~8 nm near Si or Au substrates shows disordered packing in vapor‑deposited DSA‑Ph glasses.
- Grazing‑incidence X‑ray scattering and coarse‑grained MD both confirm this interfacial length scale.
- Deposition temperature controls glass structure beyond the interfacial layer, influencing overall molecular packing.

2608.17125.title: Demonstration of a scalable all-solid-state refrigerator exploiting diffusion geometries and limiting interfacial conductances at temperatures below 1
2608.17125.summary:
- Demonstrated a scalable all‑solid‑state refrigerator with 1121 SINIS junctions that cools phonons below 1 K.
- Leveraged diffusive quasiparticle flow and engineered superconductor‑trap interfaces to suppress back‑heat leakage.
- Fabricated using W/TiW, Al₂O₃, Al, and Au, achieving measurable phonon temperature reduction in a silicon chip.

2608.17303.title: Second Harmonic Generation Spectroscopy of the Surface Charge Density Wave in the Weyl Semimetal CoSi
2608.17303.summary:
- RA‑SHG detects a surface CDW on CoSi(with T_c = 0 ± 8 K.
- SHG intensity follows a power law with β = 30 ± 03, matching 3D XY universality.
- The transition is purely surface‑driven; Fermi‑arc coupling to bulk topology imparts 3D character.

2608.17424.title: Many-Anyon Braiding in Non-Abelian Fractional Quantum Hall Effect with Hybrid Monte Carlo Simulation
2608.17424.summary:
- Hybrid Monte Carlo efficiently computes many‑anyon braiding matrices for Moore‑Read quasiholes.
- Global‑rotation braiding schemes are robust against finite‑size effects, outperforming simple two‑anyon exchanges.
- Electron interactions and local trapping potentials shift fusion‑channel energetics, altering braiding matrices and revealing long‑range entanglement.

2608.17548.title: Absence of nontrivial local conserved quantities in a class of $U(1)$-symmetric spin-1 chains
2608.17548.summary:
- No nontrivial local conserved quantities exist for U(-symmetric spin‑1 chains with vanishing quadrupolar couplings, for any k‑local operator with 3 ≤ k ≤ N/
- In a frustration‑free spin‑1 chain that spontaneously breaks U(symmetry, any local conserved quantity supported on ≤ N/2 sites is a linear combination of the identity, total S^z, and the Hamiltonian.
- The same absence of k‑local conserved quantities holds for the periodic Motzkin chain, showing symmetry breaking is driven by

2608.17558.title: Inducing metal-insulator transition via disorder in correlated kagome systems
2608.17558.summary:
- Hopping disorder plus correlations localizes electrons, reducing the critical U for a Mott transition in kagome lattices.
- Disorder weakens but does not destroy antiferromagnetic order, producing a correlated Anderson‑insulating phase.
- Phase diagram distinguishes antiferromagnetic metal, correlated Anderson insulator, and disordered Mott insulator, guiding experimental tuning.

2608.17631.title: Gauge-constrained Spinon Complexes Near Deconfined Quantum Criticality
2608.17631.summary:
- Pinned‑spin defects create controllable spinon–antispinon pairs, showing string‑breaking when dipole energy saturates with separation.
- QMC visualizes domain‑wall strings whose connectivity is governed by VBS phase offsets, spin projection, and vorticity.
- Multi‑pin patterns form robust four‑spinon complexes and extended networks that preserve global connectivity under local distortions.

2608.09644.title: A spin-bond theory unifying non-relativistic spin splitting and emergent spin-orbit textures
2608.09644.summary:
- Unifies altermagnet and p‑wave spin splitting via a spin‑bond theory separating unitary spin phases (odd‑parity, spin‑orbit‑like) and Hermitian spin amplitudes (even‑parity, altermagnetic).
- Identifies a non‑commuting regime where the two sectors mix, yielding a non‑coplanar spin texture with even‑in‑momentum transverse polarization observable by ARPES.
- Shows that geometric tuning of bond non‑commutation dynamically controls

2608.17647.title: Wavelength-Resolved Control of Photovoltaic Screening and Defect-Mediated Doping in Photo-Ferroelectric/Graphene Devices
2608.17647.summary:
- 365 nm (above‑bandgap) light induces photovoltaic screening, collapsing graphene resistance contrast from 290 % to 15 %.
- 530 nm light excites defect states, causing weaker screening and retaining higher resistance contrast.
- Graphene’s high‑gain sensing amplifies ferroelectric polarization dynamics, enabling photon‑energy‑controlled tuning of remanent polarization and doping.

2608.17745.title: Bridging ambient- and high-pressure superconductivity in La$_2$LnNi$_2$O$_7$ films
2608.17745.summary:
- Bilayer nickelate films La₂LnNi₂O₇ show Tc ≈ 41–42 K at ambient pressure, rising to 67–73 K at 16 GPa.
- Normal‑state resistivity evolves from T² (Fermi liquid) to T‑linear (non‑Fermi liquid) as Tc increases.
- Lattice compression via Ln substitution mimics pressure but actually suppresses Tc, highlighting the delicate lattice‑superconductivity interplay.

2608.17777.title: Entropy mapping under uniaxial pressure utilizing the elastocaloric effect
2608.17777.summary:
- Developed a.c. elastocaloric technique that merges low‑frequency strong‑coupling and high‑frequency quasi‑adiabatic data to recover absolute entropy and specific heat under uniaxial pressure.
- Applied to Sr₂RuO₄, mapping entropy across its phase diagram and showing maximal entropy quenching at the critical strain (Van Hove singularity).
- Determined that the specific‑heat jump Δc/(γT) at VH strain is smaller than earlier indirect estimates, revising previous caloric interpretations.

2608.18065.title: Quantum Geometric Tensor Preconditioning for Stable Training of Recurrent Neural Quantum States
2608.18065.summary:
- Demonstrates that minimum‑step stochastic reconfiguration (minSR) can be stabilized for RNN‑based Neural Quantum States via simple regularization.
- Shows minSR outperforms Adam on 1D transverse‑field Ising and cluster state, with competitive results on 2D Heisenberg and \(J_1\!-\!J_2\) models.
- Provides a pathway to apply curvature‑based optimizers to autoregressive NQS for efficient quantum simulation.
